    reflection read it, each said whether it could take the device's rays as well. First a read as a
    Reply, each form's cost by cascade on Sponza, the bounce rooms and a scene of many moving
    meshes, the structures' upkeep counted, and each against the traced reference, so the default is
    chosen on figures; the voxel game's reading of the switch as it stands today is the first of
    them. Its tests hold the two forms within a bound of each other in the rooms and run the
    device's form where the device has it, the field's on the runners. The first reading, the voxel
    game's at High on an RTX 4070 Laptop of 8 GB, recorded at 13:08 on 2026-11-14, three sessions
    under the exclusive lock, the sheet 12-37-gi-field-against-device-rays.png in the game's dump.
    The switch as it stands traces every world probe's ray through the meshes after marching it
    through the field for its reach, so it reads the field against the field and the device's rays,
    not either alone, and does not reach the screen's probes. gpu.global_illumination reads 6.02 to
    6.08 ms against 6.14 to 6.19 standing in the built room, 0.12 less, and 5.69 to 5.75 against
    5.35 to 5.39 in a flight, 0.34 more; nothing else moves past the spread. The pictures part by

    wall stands in a view. Each way stands far further from the traced reference than from the

    two ways should part.

288. **The scene field and the ray scene on the processor in a frame of a streamed world.** The

    mended, the step's work spread over frames or kept from one step to the next, with the field's

    the same scene before and after, the worst frame at a step and at a mesh's coming.

289. **The field's light moves with meshes the traced reference shows give nothing.** A game's
    reading in ASKS.md has two path traces of one place, one with every mesh and one with the meshes

    cache or the occlusion), then the mend so a surface lit from one side reads the same with or
    without what lies behind it, with a test comparing the two frames within a bound of pixels on

290. **The water mirror's first frame.** A game's reading in ASKS.md has the frame a mirror first
draws in at 34 to 41 ms under `cpu.mirror` in five runs of five, where the same frame costs 0.4 to
16 ms with fewer meshes standing in the shadow maps and the field alone, so the first frame looks to
cost by every mesh standing, those a mirror never draws among them. Asked, the first frame read by
its parts in a scene of the engine's own with some hundreds of meshes of which a share are
shadow-only (what is made once, what is walked for each mesh, what waits on the device), then the
mend, a mirror walking only what it draws and its first frame's making spread or made ahead where it
is the making that costs, the mirror's first frame and its later frames before and after in a table,
with a test on the count of meshes a mirror's pass walks. A later reading of the same game, one
flight each way, has the first frame at 16.8 against 34.2 ms with the same 819 parts drawn and 6
shadow-only, and 842 against 854 parts standing with a mesh, so the time follows neither the meshes
drawn nor those standing, and the read by parts comes before any mend, with what was made or
compiled in the frames before the first counted among the parts. No picture asked where nothing seen
changes.

292. **The ray scene grows and compacts its corners without waiting on the queue.** A game's reading
    in ASKS.md has `cpu.global_illumination` at 32.5 to 43.1 ms in the one frame where the corner
    buffer grows from 256 to 1,024 MiB past 16,777,216 corners, 3,520 to 3,851 meshes for some 700
    placed copies, and `GpuRayScene` at the head still copies through `EndSingleTimeCommands` in
    three places, the compaction among them. Asked, the growth and the compaction made with no wait
    in the frame, the copy recorded with the frame's own commands and the old buffer let go once the
    device has passed it, or the corners kept in buffers of a fixed size added one at a time so
    nothing is copied, whichever the read of the kernels' indexing favors, said in the Reply. A test
    in a scene of the engine's own that adds meshes past a growth and reads the frame's stage beside
    its neighbors, and the light the same before and after by the tests that stand. Read together
    with item 288, whose new meshes' cost at a step is the same scene's other half, 11.4 to 17.0 ms
    for 25 to 38 meshes in the game's reading. The game's later reading names the growth whole.
    `GpuRayScene.AddCorners` grows the corner buffer fourfold, to twice the next power of two of the
    corners needed, the UVs beside it, both copies alive during the copy, 256 MiB to 1,024 MiB in the frame
    the corners pass 2 to the 24th, 43 to 57 ms with the stage at 33 to 45 ms, in 5 of 10 flights,
    the others having grown during the load. The corners of a mesh that leaves are never let go,
    16.1 million at a flight's start and 18.0 million at its end for about 3,600 meshes. Asked
    beside the above, a call by which a program reserves corners ahead, as at a world's load, the
    corners of a mesh that leaves given back for the next to take, and the growth's factor said in
    the documents with the memory it holds.

293. **The circular occluders as the window's ambient occlusion by default.** Decided on 2026-11-17,
    the circular occluders are the default and the horizon pass the one chosen by name. Asked, the
    default of `AmbientOcclusionMethod` wherever it is set turned, the documents and the feature
    list saying so, the tests and references that draw with the default drawn again and each bound
    read on the three devices, a sheet of the two ways on the Sponza by day and a room lit by glow
    blocks with the difference panel, and the frame's stage of each under the exclusive lock in a
    table. The examples and a game on the package take the default with no change of their own, said
    in the release notes. Both ways pass through the one history, 0.9 of the frame before found through the camera alone, so a thing that moves by itself leaves its occlusion behind it for some frames in either. Asked with the default, a reading of that trail, a body crossing a lit floor with the camera still and the camera turning past a still one, the frames after as a strip for each way, and the circular occluders tried with a shorter history and with none, since sixteen rays and their own filter may stand without it, the default's history set by what the strips and a still frame's grain show. It comes after items 288 and 292.

294. **A frame worked out with nothing kept from the frames before, read.** The direction given on
    2026-11-17 is that the occlusion and the global illumination should ideally work each frame out
    whole, so a change of light or geometry shows in the next frame, clear and without grain. Asked,
    a reading and no mend. First the list of everything the lit picture carries across frames, each
    with how many frames it spans and what it is for, the screen probes' kept light, the cascades'
    gather over a cycle, the field's and the ray scene's making over frames, the occlusion's
    history, the bounce taken from the frame before, and temporal antialiasing where it is on. Then
    the target scene with each of them off or made whole in the frame, one at a time and all
    together, a sheet of a still frame beside the kept one with the grain measured against a traced
    reference, a strip of the frames after a light is turned off and after a wall is taken away, and
    the frame's stages in a table, on the field and on the adapter's rays. Then what count of rays
    or probes makes the frame without history as clean as the kept one, and its cost. The bounce
    beyond the first may stay a frame behind, said apart, since it is no grain. The Reply ends in
    which parts can stand without history as they are, which at a cost, and which not on this
    device.

295. **A program's first frame with a 3D view.** The game's reading of its first shown frame gives
    the render graph 654 to 823 ms, the scene's stage at 234 to 318, the cascades' at 218 to 236,
    the window's depth at 87, the field's at 61 to 103 and the lighting's block at 24 to 28. The
    field and the probes are made with four cascades in the frames that draw no 3D view and made
    again with five in the first that does, 30 and 64 ms, though the program asked for the far
    cascade from its start, and eighteen pipelines with their pools are made in that frame from the
    driver's cache. Asked, a read of which of these the engine can make before a view is first
    drawn, the field and the probes made once at the count asked for, and a call by which a program
    has a view's pipelines and pictures made ahead while it shows a loading screen, with a test in a
    scene of the engine's own that the first frame with a view makes none of them. After items 288
    and 292, whose buffers are the same scene's.

301. **The edit mesh gives way to the Modeling module's.** Shared: Modeling's item 3 part 1
    (27e2dc9) holds the edit mesh as Modeling.EditMesh, its recipe and EditMeshBuild, reading files
    through IModelFiles; an engine can bind it, its own EditMeshData, EarClipping, FaceMerge, Csg,
    SlotLook and build giving way to the module's, with the kernel tests already moved. After item
    265.

302. **The Diagnostics module takes the console, the overlay's model, the keys and the settings.**
    Both engines carry nearly the same command registry, console host and overlay model, with keys
    that drifted apart, and neither has a registry of settings. The module `3DEngine.Diagnostics`
    holds them once. In steps, each its own commit on main with the suite whole. Step 1, the
    registry. The module comes as a submodule at `modules/Diagnostics`, embedded as the other
    modules are and never a package. The `[Command]` attribute is the module's, the generator stays
    here and emits `Registry.Process.Add` as the module's README says a generator emits, and the
    engine's own command registry, its command and parameter types go; the console host runs a line
    through the module's registry, a late answer written to the console by the host; the Modeling
    module's commands are hosted through its list of commands in place of the engine's own `model.*`
    ones. Step 2, the console, the overlay and the keys. The console's model and its ImGui drawing
    are the module's, the overlay's lines come as sections the engine fills, and the keys are the
    module's actions, F1 hide the interface, F2 screenshot, F3 overlay, F4 settings panel, F5
    console, each a setting a player rebinds, no chord of F3 with F4. Step 3, the settings. Every
    engine value a console command or an environment variable sets today is registered as a setting
    with its range, its default, whether it takes effect at the next start and the variable that
    overrides it, the panel draws them by page, and a game's settings are saved to one file in the
    player's folder through the module's file. A picture of the console and of the panel in a
    running example with each of steps 2 and 3. What the module lacks for a step goes to its session
    in five lines and is mended there, never worked round here. The lighting branch goes on beside
    this.

303. **The Sky module is named Atmosphere.** The module's repository becomes 3DEngine.Atmosphere,
    its assembly and namespace Atmosphere and its class Atmosphere becomes Air, by the module's own
    item. Once the module's commit is on GitHub the engine follows in one commit. The submodule
    moves from modules/Sky to modules/Atmosphere with the new address, the project references and
    the package's embedded assembly take the name, each `using Sky;` becomes `using Atmosphere;`,
    and the type Atmosphere becomes Air where the engine names it. The engine's own names with sky
    in them, its commands and settings pages among them, stay. The guides, the cheatsheet and the
    README's module table take the name, and `docs-on-package.py` builds the guides' blocks on a
    package of that tree before the report. No behavior changes, so no picture is asked.

304. **The probe passes go on, through the module's second merge.** The branch is taken up again
    with one aim, a module the engine uses that reads nearer the reference and costs less than
    main's own passes. The module gains main's merge as a second selectable one, by its own item.
    Once that commit is on GitHub the branch takes the pin and selects it, with no merge code of its
    own left. The pass mark at the door is main's table, each of the six parts within 0.10 of main's
    ratio, the roof slab, the lintel and the open box at Low passing, and the whole GI's time at or
    under main's in both scenes. Where a part misses, one read names what the module's form of the
    merge does that main's does not, and it goes to the module's session with the figures. The first
    merge's table from 42ed4e13 stands beside it as the other half of the comparison. The branch
    lands on main when the mark is met, and the engine's own passes are deleted in that commit.

305. **Escape goes to what is open first, and leaves an example last.** The window's exit key is
    Escape by default, so with the settings panel open the key that goes back a page closes the
    example instead. Escape is handed down one order and the first taker keeps it. An open console,
    settings panel or overlay page takes it, as does a text field with the caret in it or any
    interface holding the keyboard, and the window does not see it. Where nothing is open, an
    example started from the list goes back to the list on Escape, and an example started by name
    ends. The engine's own default exit key becomes none, so a game closes by its close button, the
    system's own shortcut or a call it makes, and sets an exit key where it asks for one; the
    examples program sets its own. The rule sits in one place the window asks before it acts on the
    exit key, which the diagnostics and a game's own interface answer. Tests hold that Escape with
    the panel open goes back a page and leaves the window open, that Escape with nothing open leaves
    an example, and that a game with no exit key set stays open. The guides and the cheatsheet say
    it, and this goes ahead of the pass-hash read as a small commit of its own.

306. **An open console or settings panel holds all input from the program.** With the settings panel
    open in a scene, the pad and the keys that change a row also drive the scene, so the time of day
    moves while a setting is switched. The Diagnostics module answers whether a panel that takes
    input is open, and while it does the engine's input calls answer a program as though nothing
    were pressed or moved, keyboard, pointer, wheel and pad alike, in the loop's calls and the ECS's
    input resources both. The overlay holds nothing. The diagnostics' own keys still act, and a held
    key or stick at the moment a panel closes does not fire as a fresh press. Tests hold a pad's
    stick and a key reading as idle with the panel open and live with the overlay alone, the guides
    say it, and it comes with the module's pin as a commit of its own.

307. **The window's settings in the panel.** The settings panel holds nothing of the window itself.
    A page `window` gains `window.mode` with the choices windowed, borderless and fullscreen,
    `window.resizable`, `window.width` and `window.height` for the windowed mode as two settings,
    `window.monitor` naming the screen where more than one is there, and `window.vsync` where it is
    not listed already. A command of a setting's name gives the name to the setting. Each acts at
    once where the system allows it and says "at the next start" on its row where it does not, they
    are saved with the other settings and applied at the next start before the first frame is shown,
    and a mode the system refuses answers in the console and keeps the one before. Borderless covers
    the screen the window is on with no change of the screen's own mode, fullscreen takes the
    screen's mode. A window not shown has the page read-only. The names and choices are the same in
    both engines. Tests hold each setting's round through the file and the refusal, a sheet shows
    the page and the three modes, and the guides say it. It comes after item 306.

308. **The ambient occlusion at full size sits against the camera.** Seen in a shown window with the
    settings changed by hand, the ambient occlusion at its full size does not lie where the surfaces
    are, it moves the other way as the camera turns, as though flipped, and at half size it sits
    right and goes with the view. The first step reproduces it offscreen, a scene with clear
    corners, the camera at three turns, the occlusion alone drawn at half and at full size and their
    difference, in both occlusion modes. The cause is then named from one reading, which axis is
    turned and in which pass, the fix follows, and a test holds the two sizes equal within a bound
    after the full one is brought to the half one's size, at each turn. A sheet with the pairs
    before and after rides in the commit. It comes after item 306 and before 307.

309. **The view of the fields shows each one in a small place off the camera on one axis.** Seen in
    a shown window, the view of field 1 has content only in one small region that sits at the
    camera's place moved some way along one axis, the same whichever way the camera looks, the next
    field's region is the same and a little larger, the third larger again, and so on. A field about
    the camera would fill the view round it. The first step reproduces it offscreen with the camera
    at two places and two turns and each field's view, and says which it is, the view drawing each
    field at a wrong place or size, or the fields themselves standing off the camera, which the
    lighting would then feel, read from each field's stated center and extent beside the camera's
    place. The fix follows the reading, a test holds each field's center within one cell of the
    camera's place along every axis and the view's region equal to the field's extent, and a sheet
    before and after rides in the commit. It comes after item 308.

311. **A gather by pixel beside the screen probes, either one choosable.** The screen probes still
    flicker in a shown window after every mend, so a second way of bringing the cascades' light to
    the picture is tried beside them, and a setting chooses either. It takes its place after 307 and
    before 310. Step one reads the flicker itself, offscreen, on a still camera and on a slow turn
    in Sponza and the feature test, as the change of a pixel from frame to frame with nothing in the
    scene moving, per quality, and names its source in one reading or says it is suspected. If a
    mend follows from that reading it is made, since the probes stay where they are faster. Step two
    is the gather by pixel. Each pixel sends one ray over its hemisphere, through the distance field
    or the hardware scene as the backend is set, the hit takes its light from the cascades and
    nothing is traced past it, and a miss takes the cascades' light in that direction. It runs at
    full, half, quarter and eighth size with an upscale that follows depth and normal, whole each
    frame with no history, any filter working inside the one frame. Step three reads both ways
    against the traced reference in the two scenes, the difference, the frame to frame change of a
    still view, and the time of each at each size, on one sheet with difference panels. The Reply
    says plainly where one ray a pixel with no history is too grainy to stand and what removes the
    grain inside the frame (more rays at a smaller size, the filter's width, the cascades taken
    sooner along the ray). The setting keeps both whatever the reading says, its default the one the
    sheet favors.

312. **A borderless window takes the size set, in the screen's middle.** Borderless today covers the
whole screen whatever `window.width` and `window.height` say. A player on a large screen sets a
smaller resolution and expects a window without a frame at exactly that size, sharp and one pixel to
one pixel, standing in the middle of the screen with the desktop round it, and not a stretched
picture. So `window.mode` borderless makes a frameless window of `window.width` by `window.height`
in the middle of the screen `window.monitor` names. A size as large as the screen or larger covers
the screen as borderless does today, and that is how a player gets the covering kind. Setting the
width or the height while borderless resizes the frameless window at once and keeps it in the
middle. Windowed keeps its frame and its place, fullscreen takes the screen's mode as before. The
picture is drawn at the window's own size and never scaled to the screen. A test holds the size, the
place and the missing frame at a size under the screen's and the cover at the screen's size, and the
sheet shows a borderless window at a smaller size on a larger screen beside the covering one. The
guides and the cheatsheet say it. The mode has four choices, windowed, borderless, borderless
fullscreen and fullscreen. Borderless is the frameless window at the size set, as above, and a size
as large as the screen is the only way it covers. Borderless fullscreen is a frameless window that
always covers the screen, and it draws the picture at `window.width` by `window.height` and scales
it to the screen, so a smaller size set gives a softer picture at less cost, which some players
choose. The scaling is one filtered copy at the frame's end, with the interface drawn after it at
the screen's size where the engine has that split and with it otherwise, the Reply saying which.
This part replaces the sentence above that lets the size decide the cover between two kinds, and the
sheet shows all four. A setting `window.scaling` chooses how borderless fullscreen brings the
picture to the screen, with three choices. Linear is the filtered copy, soft. Nearest takes each
screen pixel from the one picture pixel under it, sharp, even at a whole ratio such as 1920 by 1080
on 3840 by 2160 and uneven at any other, which its help line says. Integer scales by the largest
whole number that fits and stands the picture in the screen's middle with black round it, every
picture pixel a square block of screen pixels. The default is Linear. The sheet shows the three on
one crop at a whole ratio and at a ratio of one and a half.

310. **Rough reflections from the cascades, shown in a scene.** Reflection is the next large step
    after the branch, tried rough first and whole each frame with no history. The RadianceCascades
    module's item 10 writes the kernel that reads a reflection cone from the cascades and names the
    roughness below which it parts from a traced reference. This item waits for that Reply and takes
    its place after 307. Its first step is a Reply alone, saying what the engine draws for a glossy
    surface today (which pass, from which light, with what history) and which path takes the
    module's kernel soonest, main's own cascades or the branch's shared passes. The trial then draws
    the kernel's reflection in the feature test's materials wall and in Sponza's floor, behind a
    setting that chooses it beside what stands today, and reads it against the traced reference at
    roughness 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 with a sheet of the three (today, the kernel, the reference,
    difference panels) and the pass's time at each quality. Sharp reflections by a traced ray lit
    from the cascades are a later item and are not begun here.

## Verdicts

Verdict 133 is open, the build on `cf5aa498` red on `SceneLoadedTests`' byte count in the Windows
job, suspected of the measure and not the code.

131. **The reflections' reference frame recorded again for item 299 differs on the runners.** In run
    44943683933 on `31c089de`, read at 22:56 on 2026-11-21, the reference frame test of
    `reflections.png` failed in `linux (order)`, `linux (shuffled)`, `macos (2)` and `windows (4)`,
    2.3 percent of the pixels apart against a bound of 2, within rows 47 to 137 and columns 39 to
    216, the frame's gray a few levels over the reference's; every other job passed. The frame was
    recorded again on the desktop's card with the roughness widened across a pixel, and the software
    devices and the other systems draw that widening a little apart. Read the frame on lavapipe in
    the runner's image and on the Windows device as the norm's recipe gives it, name what parts by
    device (the derivative of the normal at an edge, the samples a pixel), and mend it there or
    record the frame so that each device stands within the bound by a count of pixels, the bound
    itself not widened. Settled when a run passes the frame on the three systems.

133. **The build on `cf5aa498` is red on one test in the Windows job's second part.** Read at 04:11
    on 2026-11-23 from the job's log, run 45090396893. `SceneLoadedTests` compares the bytes a
    scene's load takes with an observer of another thing against the bytes with none and asks them
    equal, 2,544 expected and 2,704 found, 160 apart. The commit changed a module pin and a window
    test and nothing in a scene's load, and the runs on `a1bf0fc5` and before passed, so the test's
    measure is suspected of moving with the runtime on that runner and not the code. The mend makes
    the test hold on what it means, the least of several takes on each side or a bound in place of
    equal bytes, and says in its Reply how often it failed in twenty local runs before and after.
    The verdict settles on a green run with the mend.

## Decisions

Decisions 1 Commits stay local; 2 The package is `3DEngine` on nuget.org, the owner's own, numbered
from 5.0; 3 AGENTS.md's bullet and table row on SHARED.md change by the project's direction alone; 4
TODO.md's two Entities entries are closed as decided; 5 A commit that takes something out of the
public surface is numbered by the project's direction; 6 AGENTS.md's bullet and table row on NORM.md
change by the project's direction alone, with the exception N 7.4 makes; 7 A run that fails says
what failed in a page, and the reviewing session is given no log; 8 The page's repeated lines are
warnings and errors; 9 `GetFontDefault` stays ImGui's ProggyClean; 10 A render texture takes the
window's samples; 11 The package ships no ReadyToRun images, the author's own publish being the way;
12 Per-object motion blur and ImGui viewports are wanted, after the standing items; 13 Audio falls
back to a device of silence where there is none; 14 A document a game's author reads names no one
who decided; 15 Text is shaped whole; 16 Global illumination comes in four phases, a scene distance
field first; 17 Every tonemapper BevyCSharp offers is in 3DEngine; 18 Subsurface scattering is the
next large item, the first of Decision 16's spectral experiments; 19 5.2 is packed when every job is
green, before subsurface scattering lands; 20 Three packages are bumped after 5.2; 21 The animated
model's meshes in the world follow subsurface scattering; 22 The bounce's quality comes before
subsurface scattering goes on; 23 No document or comment a reader sees names a person or a session;
24 Content streamed on the go stays in the ledger, and the browser waits for a game that asks; 25 A
run that shows no window makes no sound; 26 A game's session writes what the engine lacks in
`.github/ASKS.md`; 27 A look on 2026-10-10 opens item 2 again, four things seen; 28 Seen on
2026-10-11, the sky's light leaking into the game's cave by the heading is a glitch to be found and
fixed, and the overlay gains a post-processing window; 29 The README's gallery is one scrolling row
of pictures a folder, sorted by folder, and the games' text under the table goes; 30 The e3d skill
leaves `.claude` for `.github/E3D.md`, and the gallery's pictures are one size; 31 `games/Pusher`
goes; 32 The GPU named nowhere a user reads, `Engine3D` renamed `E3D`, and the guide table opening
with the cheatsheet; 33 The radiance cascades are said in the README and in a guide page of their
own; 34 The examples' counts stand under the Examples heading and on each folder's heading; 35 A
push plays one game, and the pack run plays them all; 36 A vertex stream of the game's own, in both
engines; 37 A position is every mesh's, and the packed data a stream beside it; 38 The macOS
captures run in the pack run alone; 39 No development on either engine until every job is green on
every push and pack; 40 Two workflows an engine, build and pack, the same shape in both; 41 The
voxel game moves to its own repository, Voxel-Sandbox, and a tiny sample stays under `games/`; 42
Decision 39's gate is the new workflows; 43 Prose is technical and generic; 44 Development resumes
on all three fronts, the radiance cascades first; 45 The README's centered parts are markdown inside
a centering block, since nuget.org draws a README without its HTML; 46 The code fixes project stays;
47 A package's release notes are the commits since the package last published on nuget.org; 48 The
pack workflow publishes through nuget.org's trusted publishing; 49 The reviewer starts the pack runs
when a package is due; 50 The review's files are committed by the batch that comes next, and by the
reviewer at most once a day; 51 Modeling in both engines, from the kernel to the modifiers, grid
prototyping first; 52 The Actions bill is not weighed; 53 Animated captures as tooling for

Verdict 133, the byte count of a load no one observes.

What moves by 160 bytes is the load's debug line. `SceneFile.Read` logs that it spawned 3 entities,
and `Logger` hands the line to the file log once an app in the process has begun the file, and not
before that nor once the file is full. The line it builds, its time, level and category before the
message, is 69 characters, a string of 160 bytes. On the Windows job's second part a test beside
this one opened an app between the reads of the world without an observer and those with one, so
each read after took the line's bytes. Opening the file log between the two sets of reads in a test
of this layout reads 2,632 bytes without an observer and 2,792 with one, 160 apart, in 3 runs of 3.
The registry's lookup building its index again for a codec registered beside it is the other change
of the same kind that the least of several was there for.

The mend reads two worlds in pairs, one without an observer and one with an observer of something
else, and holds that at least one of five pairs reads the same. A change of the process's state
between a pair's two reads parts that pair alone, and an observer that made the load do more would
part all five. Opening the file log partway through this layout leaves 4 pairs of 5 equal in 3 runs
of 3. The scenes' tests failed in 0 of 20 local runs before the mend and 0 of 20 after, since a
local run starts no app beside them. The whole suite passes, 2,560 tests.

Item 312, the four window modes and borderless fullscreen's scaling.

`window.mode` takes `Windowed`, `Borderless`, `BorderlessFullscreen` and `Fullscreen`, the names
BevyCSharp takes. Borderless is a window with no frame of `window.width` by `window.height` in the
middle of the screen `window.monitor` names, and covers that screen at its size or larger. Setting
the width or the height while it is borderless resizes it at once and keeps it in the middle.
Windowed takes back the frame, the size and the place a borderless window gave up, which SDL keeps
of a window only across its own fullscreen. `ToggleBorderlessWindowed` is borderless at its
monitor's size, so it covers and draws at the monitor's resolution, and gives the window back its
size as it toggles off.

Borderless fullscreen always covers. Where the size set is not the screen's, the device draws the
frames into images of its own at that size, one to each of the swapchain's, and at the end of the
frame one blit copies the frame onto the swapchain's image, cleared to black round it, before the
present. At the screen's own size the frames are drawn into the swapchain's images with no copy.
The interface is drawn with the picture, into the frame image, since the 2D batch and ImGui draw in
the window's pass after the composite, and a split would need every pass to take a scene size
apart from the window's. The program is given the size drawn at, in `GetScreenWidth`,
`GetRenderWidth`, the cameras' aspect and ImGui's display size, and the pointer's place, its
motion, a finger's place and `SetMousePosition`'s warp go through where the frame stands on the
screen. Linear and Nearest keep the frame's shape, as large as fits with black round it, rather
than stretch it onto a screen of another shape. On a screen with more pixels than points the frame
is the size set times the window's pixels to a point, the pixels a window of that size has. A
surface that cannot be copied into draws at the screen's size and says so in the log. `shot` and
the captures read the frame as drawn, and `shot.shown` reads it as the screen shows it, which the
sheet is made from.

`window.scaling` is `Linear` by default, filtered and soft, `Nearest`, sharp, even at a whole ratio
and uneven otherwise, which its help says, and `Integer`, the largest whole multiple that fits,
centered with black round it, and as Linear where the frame is larger than the screen. It is kept
in the settings file and given before the window is shown.

`A_Borderless_Window_Takes_The_Size_Set_In_The_Middle_Of_Its_Screen_And_Covers_It_At_The_Screens_Size`
holds the size, the place and the missing frame at 320 by 240 and at 400 by 240, the cover at the
screen's size, and borderless fullscreen covering at any size. SDL's offscreen driver places no
window and draws no frame, so the suite holds the size and the cover there, and the test holds the
place and the frame on SDL's X11 driver in a headless mutter through Xwayland, as
`E3D_TEST_VIDEO_DRIVER=x11` runs it, where all six window tests pass.
`Borderless_Fullscreen_Draws_At_The_Size_Set_And_Scales_It_Onto_Its_Screen_As_Window_Scaling_Says`
holds the frame drawn at 300 by 200, the offscreen screen's 1024 by 768 shown with the frame at
each scaling's place, black round it, and the pointer at the frame's corner and middle landing on
its first pixel and its middle. On Wayland the system places each window itself, so a borderless
window stands where it puts it, which the guide says.

The sheet `.github/assets/readings/2026-11-23-item-312-window-modes.webp` shows the four modes on a
screen of 1920 by 1080, and the three scalings on one crop of the camera's help at 960 by 540, a
ratio of 2, and at 1280 by 720, a ratio of 1.5. At 2 Nearest and Integer are the same pixels and
Linear is soft, and at 1.5 Nearest's columns are uneven and Integer draws at 1. The run that made
it reported no validation errors. The whole suite passes, 2,562 tests, the settings' test counting
the window page's eighth setting and the file keeping it.
